parts.technique: Factor/remainder theorem, polynomial manipulation
parts.reason: Uses the factor/remainder theorem on a cubic polynomial, covered by P2.6 (factorisation, use of the factor theorem) and polynomial manipulation.

parts.technique: Binomial expansion, coefficient of a term
parts.reason: Finding a coefficient in a binomial expansion (a+bx)^n for positive integer n is directly covered by P4.1.

parts.label: 3a
parts.technique: Equation of a circle
parts.reason: Finding the equation of a circle given centre and a point uses P3.2 (equation of a circle, radius).

parts.label: 3b
parts.technique: Circle geometry - chord parallel to axis
parts.reason: Uses circle properties (perpendicular from centre bisects chord) and Pythagoras, covered by P3.2.

parts.label: 4a
parts.technique: Sketching exponential-type curve with transformation and asymptote
parts.reason: Sketching y = a^(-x)+4 requires understanding of exponential graphs (P6.1) and transformations/asymptotes (P2.7/P2.9), all in spec.

parts.label: 4b
parts.technique: Trapezium rule
parts.reason: Direct application of the trapezium rule with given table of values, covered by P9.4.

parts.label: 4c
parts.technique: Manipulating a definite integral using linearity/splitting range, building on trapezium rule estimate
parts.reason: Part (c) asks students to use the numerical estimate from (b) together with linearity of definite integrals (subtracting a linear term, or adding an integral over an adjacent interval) to approximate related integrals. Both underlying skills — the trapezium rule (P9.4) and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus / properties of definite integrals (P8.1) — are in spec, and the part depends on the in-spec answer to (b), so it remains in spec.

parts.label: 5i
parts.technique: Sum to infinity of a geometric series
parts.reason: Directly covered by P4.5 (sum to infinity of a convergent geometric series).

parts.label: 5iia
parts.technique: Recurrence relation, periodic sequence
parts.reason: Sequence defined by x_{n+1}=f(x_n) and showing periodicity is explicitly covered by P4.2.

parts.label: 5iib
parts.technique: Stating order of a periodic sequence
parts.reason: Periodic sequences and their order are explicitly named in P4.2's guidance (periodic sequence of order 2 example).

parts.label: 5iic
parts.technique: Summing terms of a periodic sequence using sigma notation
parts.reason: Uses sigma notation (P4.3) together with the periodic sequence result from (a)/(b); both are in-spec topics and the part follows from in-spec earlier parts.

parts.label: 6a
parts.technique: Laws of logarithms to derive a polynomial equation
parts.reason: Uses laws of logarithms (P6.4) combined with algebraic manipulation of polynomials (P2.6); no excluded content.

parts.label: 6bi
parts.technique: Solving a cubic using a known root (factor theorem) and quadratic formula
parts.reason: Uses factor theorem/algebraic division (P2.6) and solving a quadratic equation (P2.3).

parts.label: 6bii
parts.technique: Selecting valid solution to original log equation
parts.reason: Uses the roots found in (b)(i) (in spec) and log domain restriction (P6.3); depends on in-spec earlier work.

parts.label: 7a
parts.technique: Arithmetic sequence modelling
parts.reason: Finding nth term of an arithmetic sequence given two terms, covered by P4.4 and P4.6 (modelling).

parts.label: 7b
parts.technique: Geometric sequence modelling
parts.reason: Finding nth term of a geometric sequence given two terms, covered by P4.5 and P4.6.

parts.label: 7c
parts.technique: Sum of arithmetic and geometric series, comparison
parts.reason: Uses sum formulae for arithmetic and geometric series, covered by P4.4/P4.5.

parts.label: 8i
parts.technique: Disproof by counter-example
parts.reason: Explicitly named method in P1.1 with a directly analogous example given in the guidance.

parts.label: 8ii
parts.technique: Proof by exhaustion (algebraic, odd/even cases)
parts.reason: Explicitly named method in P1.1, with guidance example of proof by exhaustion for a similar number-theory statement.

parts.label: 9i
parts.technique: Solving trig equation using tan=sin/cos and Pythagorean identity, quadratic in cos
parts.reason: Uses P5.5 identities and P5.7 (quadratic trig equations) and P2.3 (solving quadratics); all in spec.

parts.label: 9iia
parts.technique: Identifying amplitude/constant from transformed sine graph
parts.reason: Understanding transformations of sin function (P2.9) and trig graphs (P5.3).

parts.label: 9iib
parts.technique: Exact trig values from transformed sine function
parts.reason: Requires exact sin/cos values at standard angles (P5.3) combined with transformations, in spec.

parts.label: 9iic
parts.technique: Solving trig equation with transformed argument using arcsin
parts.reason: Solving trig equations with multiples/transformations of the angle is covered by P5.7 and use of arcsin by P5.4.

parts.label: 10a
parts.technique: Differentiation of x^n (rational powers) to find stationary point
parts.reason: Directly covered by P7.2 (differentiate x^n for rational n) and P7.3 (stationary points).

parts.label: 10b
parts.technique: Algebraic integration of x^n (rational powers) to find area between curve and line
parts.reason: Directly covered by P8.2 (integrate x^n) and P8.3 (area under/between curves using definite integrals).
